The solution is written. Summary of what I produced:

**`/workspace`** covers all 36 query frames (12 per clip × 3 clips), each with 20 `[x,y,z]` joint rows in metres in the RGB camera frame.

**Approach** (given the no-tools ablation — only 4 of the 12 queried frames per clip had pasted still images):
- I read every provided PNG and located the **right hand** in each. Right-hand poses seen: clip_01 gripping a mug/mouse/dumbbell (fist-like grips) low-right in frame; clip_02 pressing a phone against a screen and holding a mug (fist grips); clip_03 reaching over a keyboard, holding a mug, and gripping a Rubik's cube.
- For each visible right hand I estimated the **wrist pixel**, an approximate **depth Z** (~0.3–0.46 m, from apparent hand size in the frame), and an in-plane **rotation**, then back-projected the wrist through the pinhole intrinsics (`fx=fy=500`, `cx=cy=511.5`) and hung a parametric 20-joint hand skeleton (open-palm or closed-grip template) off it.
- For the **8 unseen query frames per clip** I placed a plausible neutral right-hand pose (hand near lower-right of view at ~0.4 m), consistent with the observed tabletop manipulation context.

These are rough estimates — the seen frames are grounded in real image evidence, the unseen ones are reasonable priors — giving complete coverage of every query as required.
